name: Michri
overview: Michri is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily as the father of Uzzi. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or distinguishing events recorded. He serves as a genealogical link within the Benjaminite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Michri appears as a proper name in Scripture without any given meaning or divine attribution. It is simply recorded as the name of this Benjaminite individual in 1 Chronicles 9:8.
familyAndRelationships: Michri is explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin and is noted as the father of Uzzi. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details concerning Michri.
scriptureSignificance: Michri's significance lies in his role within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, as documented in 1 Chronicles 9:8. His mention helps preserve the lineage and heritage important to the biblical narrative, contributing to the broader understanding of Israelite ancestry. Though not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the value Scripture places on preserving family lines.
